A note-writing rule from the Zettelkasten tradition: each note holds one idea, written so it makes sense without its neighbours.

## Why one idea

A note with three ideas can only be linked as a whole, so a link that wants one of them drags in the other two. Splitting lets each idea be cited where it is needed, as on the cards of the [[zettelkasten]].

## Written for a stranger

The rule asks for complete sentences and the source named in the note, because the reader months later will not remember the context.

## What I said reading it

One idea per note is a rule about linking, not about length.
